scope: Proposition 7.1 (Routes with rare encounters away from the common end) of the manuscript “Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas” (preprints/Quantum-Depletion-and-Momentum-Distribution-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas-October-5-2026/Quantum-Depletion-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e8a9907a3ac0811), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are p0, κ, c, C > 0 and R0 with the following property. Suppose R ≥ R0, K ≥ C0R, and (7.1) holds with p ≤ p0. Put h = ⌊R1/2⌋. There is an event E, determined by D, z, Q, on which the construction below gives simple good nearest-neighbor routes πy from z to every y ∈ Q. Conditional on the datum, routes are sampled using fresh independent random variables. The event includes the requirement that the 10R-neighborhoods of z and Q contain no bad sites. For a route π = (v0, . . . , vm) starting at z, set a(π) = max{i : d∞(vi, z) ≤ h}, πch = {vi : i > a(π)}. Its silent portion (v0, . . . , va(π)) has at most Ch vertices. The analogous silent portion read backwards from y also has at most Ch vertices, and the two portions are disjoint. Let πch,q consist of vertices whose path index is within q of an index in πch. For independently sampled routes πy, πy′ , define J = X v∈πy X v′∈πy′ 1{d∞(v,v′)≤rc}, J∗ = X v∈πch,q y X v′∈πch,q y′ 1{d∞(v,v′)≤rc}. For every fixed pair y, y′ ∈ Q, ED h 1E Eroutes(eκJ | D) i ≤ C. (7.2) For every deterministic probability mass function ω on Q × Q satisfying ω(y, y′) ≤ CωR−6, X y,y′∈Q ω(y, y′ ) ED[1E Proutes(J∗ > 0 | D)] ≤ CCωR−cg , cg = 1 2  log 2 log 3 − 1 2  > 0. (7.3) The same conclusions hold with a common terminal endpoint, reading the routes in reverse order. If M denotes just the stated bad-free margin event, then P(M \ E) ≤ K3 (Ap)⌊K/(10(rc+2))⌋ + CR3 e−cR . (7.4) Here A is fixed and p0 is chosen so that Ap0 < 1.
